solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Terrible suffering comes with flings being reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to fling something is to hurl or toss it

explanation.surface: Someone's affairs have been exposed in the press and the result is misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flings' looks like romantic affairs, but it is the verb: hurls.
explanation.definitionFit: In the throes of something means in the midst of violent pain or struggle, so throes are agonising spasms.

clue.text: Ring on one nameless bird

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so it is written first

parts.note: a hoop is a ring or circular band

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so a nameless word loses that letter

parts.note: taken as written before its letter is removed

explanation.surface: A ring is fitted on an unidentified bird, as a bird-ringer might do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' takes N (name) out of ONE, leaving OE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested pinkish bird of Europe, Asia and Africa, named for its call.

clue.text: Uncontrollable, like a bowler's delivery say

definitions.meaning: in cricket the bowler releases the ball from the hand, so the delivery comes from there

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler is the player who throws the ball at the batsman; each throw is a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation that has got beyond control is idiomatically said to be this; literally, a thrown ball leaves the hand.

clue.text: Stretched horizontal support, sturdy externally

indicators.note: the word for sturdy sits on the outside, wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: stout means strong and solidly built
a rung is a horizontal bar of a ladder supporting the foot

explanation.surface: A builder describes a cross-beam that was stretched into place, strong on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread out in a long thin line or extended over time is described with this phrasal adjective.

clue.text: Form of illumination minimal with peacekeepers going in

indicators.note: the peacekeepers are placed inside the word for minimal

parts.note: slight means very small or minimal
UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: A dim light is arranged as troops of a peace mission move in.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight from our star is a natural kind of illumination.

clue.text: Mark scheme within school

indicators.note: the scheme goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: a plot is a secret scheme

explanation.surface: A teacher describes the grading scheme used inside a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a grade in the surface; here it is a stain or blot.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a large irregular stain or blotch, a kind of mark.

clue.text: It's good coming in as nature intended — a bit of encouragement needed?

indicators.note: the letter for good enters the word for naked

parts.note: a jocular phrase for naked, without clothes

explanation.surface: A naturist wonders whether someone needs a little prompting to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle push or prod given to urge someone on is a small encouragement.

clue.text: That is short time after the day ruler fell

indicators.note: the time letter is placed after the day, so it comes second

parts.note: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March
T is the short form, the abbreviation, of time

explanation.surface: A historical note: that is, a short while after the day the ruler was overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruler is Julius Caesar, killed on the Ides (15th) of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, abbreviated i.e., means 'that is' in English.

clue.text: Parochial countryman has some stirring inside, being this when away?

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes inside the word for the countryman

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated provincial person

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of the word some

explanation.surface: A small-minded rustic feels some emotion stirring within when he is far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' signals an anagram of the clue word some; the definition is a cryptic hint at a person far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pining for their own house and family while absent is in this state.

clue.text: Mark tackling first bit of chemistry exam of higher degree?

indicators.note: the mark takes on, holds, the next letter inside it

parts.note: a dot is a small mark

indicators.note: only the opening letter of chemistry is used

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A grade is given for the opening part of a chemistry examination at an advanced level.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is a higher degree, so this adjective describes something relating to it.

clue.text: Starry-eyed with little energy in the morning — outside it's dull

indicators.note: the word for dull sits on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: dry means uninteresting or dull
E is the abbreviation for energy
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A romantic feels sluggish first thing and the weather outside is grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idealistic, lost in pleasant fantasies, is to be starry-eyed.

clue.text: Scientist puts what's rotten into waste container

indicators.note: the word for rotten is put inside the container

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: A researcher throws spoilt food into the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: BOFFIN is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial British term for a research scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: Paper agreements with a twist in the tail

indicators.note: only the tail, the last two letters, are turned round

parts.note: treaties are formal agreements between states

explanation.surface: A document of agreements contains a surprise ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a twist in the tail' swaps the final ES of TREATIES to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written discourse, and paper here means an academic essay.

clue.text: A politician's current measure

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician's present policy is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present' but is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the unit of electric current, short form amp.

clue.text: House next door with troublesome parental echo

indicators.note: troublesome letters are disorderly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Neighbours' house resounds with the noise of difficult parents.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs in the Commons traditionally refer to the House of Lords, next door, by this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary convention for the other chamber of the UK Parliament, the adjoining House.

clue.text: Appreciating authentic one with enthusiasm

parts.note: real means genuine or authentic
I is the Roman numeral for one
zing means energy or zest

explanation.surface: Someone genuine values things with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Realizing means coming to understand or appreciate a fact.

clue.text: What might have brought food to queen is taken in the wrong direction

parts.note: Leda, queen of Sparta in myth; belonging to her is Leda's
a tray carries food to someone

explanation.surface: A servant's tray brings dinner to the queen but goes the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: Leda was the Spartan queen seduced by Zeus as a swan; 'Leda's tray' is what might bring her food.
explanation.definitionFit: To be led astray is to be misled, guided down the wrong path.

clue.text: Transport system has men without number getting post brought round

indicators.note: the post is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: mail is the post

indicators.note: without means outside here: the men surround the number

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A railway is staffed by a few men and has its post delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'brought round' likewise wraps the post around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway running on a single track is a kind of transport system.

clue.text: Example of excellence set by top Olympian showing yellow flag?

definitions.text: Example of excellence set by top Olympian
definitions.meaning: a benchmark of excellence, as a gold medallist sets
gold is yellow and a standard is a flag

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a yellow (gold) flag (standard).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a benchmark of excellence; the monetary system tied to gold gave it that sense.

clue.text: Problem with bottomless cesspool

indicators.note: losing the bottom, the last letter, of the word

parts.note: a sump is a pit where waste water collects

explanation.surface: A bottomless cesspit causes a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem set to a pupil.

clue.text: King's mistress carries bat out for game

indicators.note: the mistress holds the other letters inside her name

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of bat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal mistress brings a bat out for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn, actress and orange-seller, was Charles II's best-known mistress; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team ball game, popular in British schools, like basketball without dribbling.

clue.text: Throw away drug in grate

parts.note: to scrap something is to discard it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone discards drugs into the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace, but it is the verb: to rasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape and to grate both mean rubbing harshly against a surface.

clue.text: Party curtailed with chaps getting in paper

parts.note: do is informal for a party

indicators.note: the chaps enter the word for curtailed

parts.note: cut means shortened or curtailed
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A party is cut short while the men get the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper or official record is a document.

clue.text: Club president being deposed, say

indicators.note: the president is removed from office, so the letter leaves

parts.note: a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A club president is ousted from office.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say or voice something.

clue.text: Set of principles? This is ultimately deficient in the City

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London

indicators.note: deficient means falling short, and ultimately says it is the very end of the word that is missing

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A moral code is found wanting in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; EC is its postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral code, a body of guiding principles.

clue.text: Little creature attached to religious group

parts.note: in can mean attached, as in 'in with' a crowd
a sect is a religious faction

explanation.surface: A small being joins a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are tiny six-legged creatures.

clue.text: Dance as you'd expect to see outside university

indicators.note: the slang word goes around the university letter

parts.note: natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: Naturally, a dance is held outside the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautch is a traditional Indian dance performed by professional dancers.

clue.text: A holy heretic in a place that has a buzz?

definitions.text: in a place that has a buzz?

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, holy
an Arian followed Arius's heresy

explanation.surface: A pious heretic visits a lively venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzz' suggests excitement, but means the hum of bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiarian means relating to beehives, places that hum with bees.

clue.text: White-collar class to which belong two men

parts.note: CL is the abbreviation for class
Eric is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: Two men belong to the office-worker class.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical work is office work, the white-collar trade.

clue.text: Energy's gushing out with new steam source

indicators.note: gushing scatters the letters while out removes the other piece

explanation.surface: Energy gushes out of a fresh source of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N from ENERGYS and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a spring throwing up hot water and steam.
